uncited: It differs from single-isosurface methods by managing independent triangle lists for each threshold [Multi-Isosurface Extraction](1162-multi-isosurface-extraction.md), dynamically selecting isovales based on adjacent material types [Generalized Marching Cubes](8320-generalized-marching-cubes.md), or transforming boundary hyper-octants into higher-dimensional simplices to prevent topological ambiguities [STEVE (Space-Time-Enclosing Volume Extraction)](10398-steve-space-time-enclosing-volume-extraction.md).

All children build on [Marching Cubes Lookup and Configuration](2518-marching-cubes-lookup-and-configuration.md), which provides the `edgeTable` and `triangleTable` derived from the 256 possible binary configurations of a voxel's eight corner signs relative to an isovalue [Lookup Table and Ambiguity Handling](10327-lookup-table-and-ambiguity-handling.md).
An extension of Marching Cubes into the fourth dimension.

The concept of multi-isosurface extraction was developed to address the need for visualizing multiple thresholds from a single dataset, as described in early implementations using node-based linked lists for triangle storage [Multi-Isosurface Extraction](1162-multi-isosurface-extraction.md).

They demonstrated that extending Marching Cubes to 4D required a look-up table with 222 configurations after symmetry removal and provided a mathematical proof for the validity of the topological structures in ambiguous cases [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that extending Marching Cubes to 4D required a look-up table with 222 configurations after symmetry removal and provided a mathematical proof for the validity of topological structures in ambiguous cases. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly confirms both points: it states that 'by extending MC into 4 dimensions the look-up table, following removal of symmetrical configurations, required 222 separate configurations' and that 'a mathematical proof of correctness is provided to verify that the topological structures generated are valid' in the context of dealing with ambiguous configurations.
